subject: Staged traffic rollout & KV priming plan for Acme private deployment
messages:
From: Jessica Lin <jessica@acme-logistics.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment cutover - traffic ramp and KV warmup questions

Laura —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are aiming to flip traffic to the VPC/private deployment during our maintenance window on Dec 8 (02:00–05:00 UTC). Before we lock the window we need a concise, actionable plan for two things: a) staged traffic ramp (percentages, timelines, metrics to watch) and b) KV cache priming / warmup so we don’t have a large latency spike on first production traffic.

Can you share a short plan and who will own the bridge and the roll-back triggers? Also attaching our internal preflight checklist for reference.

Attachments: acme_preflight_checklist.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

Thanks,
Jessica Lin
Infrastructure Eng Lead — Acme Logistics

On behalf of: ops-acme@acme-logistics.com
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Jessica Lin <jessica@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment cutover - traffic ramp and KV warmup questions

Jessica —

Thanks for the clear ask. Outlined below is a concise, operational plan we will execute during your maintenance window. I’ve kept it high signal and listed owners; Marcus and Karthik will add technical runbook snippets after this.

Plan summary (owners in parens):
- Phase 0 — Pre-window validation (T-minus 2 hours) (Marcus): run smoke suite against staging mirror, confirm KV shard allocation and SSE keys, validate monitoring/alerting hooks.
- Phase 1 — Canary (t=0) (Marcus): route 0.5% of production traffic for 15 minutes. Target checks: 99th percentile latency <= 2.0x baseline, error rate < 0.1%.
- Phase 2 — Slow ramp (t=+15 to +90 minutes) (Karthik): increase to 5% for 30 minutes, then 20% for 45 minutes. Monitor request rate, p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and inference queue depth.
- Phase 3 — Full traffic (t=+90 to +180 minutes) (Laura lead): move to 100% once stability gates pass for two consecutive windows (30m each).

KV cache priming (Marcus lead):
- Objective: ensure hot prefixes and common session keys are present in KV shards before they receive production traffic.
- Approach: run warmup jobs that iterate a prioritized list of top-100 prompt prefixes and top-1000 session contexts. Warmup runs in parallel across shards with concurrency limit = 8 workers/shard. Expected priming time: ~20–45 mins per shard depending on sequence lengths.
- Validation: smoke queries with golden prompts; confirm KV hit rate target >= 85% and median latency improvement vs cold run.

Monitoring & rollback triggers (Laura):
- Hard rollback: any sustained error spike above 2% for 10 minutes OR p99 latency > 5x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Soft hold: pause ramp if p95 latency increases 1.5x baseline for a sustained 15 minutes; investigate.

Bridge ownership and contacts:
- Bridge owner (operations/primary): laura.bennett@redwood.com (overall go/no-go)
- Runtime & KV ops: marcus.lin@redwood.com (scripts, priming)
- Networking & routing: karthik.iyer@redwood.com (BGP/VPC peers, routing cuts)

Attachments: kv-warmup-plan.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — detailed warmup script and shard concurrency recommendations.

I’ll mark up the checklist you sent and we’ll run the warmup in the pre-window slot. Marcus — can you add the concrete runbook items (commands and monitoring queries) below?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jessica Lin <jessica@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T12:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment cutover - traffic ramp and KV warmup questions

Forwarding the runbook snippet we will execute as part of Phase 0/1 preflight and warmup. Copy/paste friendly.

--- RUNBOOK EXCERPT ---
1) Preflight smoke (run from redwood-runbooks host):
- curl -fsS https://staging-acme.private/health || exit 2
- make smoke-run TARGET=acme-staging SUITE=minimal

2) KV priming job (parallel workers per shard):
- python warmup/prime_kv.py --config warmup-acme.json --workers 8 --shard-list shards.txt
- warmup log location: /var/log/redwood/warmup/acme/{timestamp}.log

3) Validation queries (Datadog/Apollo dashboard IDs included):
- Datadog query: avg:last_5m:trace.redwood.inference.latency{env:acme} by {quantile}
- KV hit rate: max:rollup(avg, 5m):kv.hits / kv.lookups{env:acme} >= 0.85

4) Smoke tests (quick list):
- 5x golden prompts (low token) -> expect p95 < 800ms
- 3x long-sequence prompts (8k tokens) -> p95 < 2.5s
- Auth/ACL checks: verify request principal maps to tenancy id

5) Rollback commands (if hard rollback triggered):
- rback traffic: redwood-routing set --target acme --route previous-hosts --force
- revoke warmup jobs: pkill -f prime_kv.py; clear stale KV locks: /usr/local/bin/kv-unlock --all
--- END RUNBOOK EXCERPT ---

I’ll publish the exact Datadog dashboard links and the warmup config into the INF-4392 ticket today. We should plan a short rehearsal Thursday (Dec 3) to exercise the warmup job against an isolated shard.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Runtime & Ops — Redwood Inference
